text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or a feeling of fullness in one ear during or after the episode? Also, were you turning your head or changing position when the vertigo started?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the sudden onset and your vascular risk factors, I need to rule out a central cause like a stroke. Do you have any difficulty with speech, swallowing, or coordination, such as stumbling or dropping things?

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the episode was brief and resolved, I need to check for positional triggers. REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike Manoeuvre.
